title: Introduction to Food Science
description: (AGRI 1329) Introduction to Food Science. The fundamental biological, chemical and physical scientific principles associated with the study of foods; topics include food composition and nutrition, food additives and regulations, food safety and toxicology, food processing, food engineering, food biotechnology, product development and sensory evaluation.

title: Horizons in Nutrition and Food Science
description: Introduction to nutrition and food science career opportunities through presentations by nutrition and food science researchers and industry professionals; addresses issues of professionalism including portfolio development, teamwork, and critical thinking skills.
prerequisites: Cross Listing: NUTR 210/FSTC 210 .

title: Introduction to Fermentation and Brewing Sciences
description: Master fermentation and brewing science, from microbial selection to bio-separation, ensuring food safety and quality compliance.

title: Directed Studies
description: Directed study of selected problems in the area of food science.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Approval of instructor; 2.0 GPR in major and overall.

title: Special Topics in...
description: Selected topics in an identified area of food science and technology. May be repeated for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Approval of instructor.

title: Research
description: Research conducted under the direction of faculty member in food science and technology. May be repeated 2 times for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Freshman or sophomore classification and approval of department head.
repeatability: May be repeated 2 times for credit.

title: Religious and Ethnic Foods
description: Understanding religious and ethnic foods with application to product development, production, and nutritional practices; emphasis on different food rules and priorities with attention given to different religious and ethnic groups within the US and around the world.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor; basic knowledge of food science and nutrition helpful. Cross Listing: NUTR 300/FSTC 300 .

title: Fundamentals of Baking
description: Chemical and physical properties of ingredients; methods of baking different products; fundamental reactions in dough fermentation and oven baking; creating healthier options of baked products.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: CHEM 222 , CHEM 227 , or CHEM 257 , or approval of instructor.

title: Principles of Food Processing
description: Principles and practices of canning, freezing, dehydration, pickling and specialty food manufacture; fundamental concepts of various techniques of preparation, processing, packaging and use of additives; processing plants visited.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: FSTC 201 ; junior or senior classification or approval of department head or instructor.

title: Food Chemistry
description: The fundamental and relevant chemistry and functionality of the major food constituents (water, carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, phytochemical nutraceuticals) and study of food emulsion systems, acids, enzymes, gels, colors, flavors and toxins.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: FSTC 201 ; CHEM 227 and CHEM 237 , or CHEM 257 or approval of instructor.

title: Food Chemistry Laboratory
description: Laboratory exercises investigating specific molecules, such as food acids, enzymes, pigments and flavors, and chemical interactions in foods, such as oxidation reactions, emulsion systems, and functional properties from a fundamental chemistry rather than an analytical perspective.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FSTC 201 ; CHEM 227 and CHEM 237 , or CHEM 257 or approval of instructor.

title: Food Analysis
description: Selected standard methods for assay of food components; principles and methodology of both classical and instrumental techniques for food analysis.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FSTC 201 ; FSTC 311 ; CHEM 227 and CHEM 237 , or CHEM 257 , or approval of instructor.

title: Food Process Engineering Technology
description: Elementary mechanics, physical and thermal properties of food and processing materials, heat transfer, mass and energy balances, psychrometrics (properties of air), insulation.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in PHYS 201 or PHYS 206 , or approval of instructor. Cross Listing: AGSM 315/FSTC 315 .

title: Food Biomanufacturing and Cellular Agriculture
description: Exploration of fermentation science, cellular agriculture, alternative proteins, and lab techniques for bioprocessing, microbial communities, and food safety.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification.

title: Molecular Microbial Detection and Characterization
description: The overall objective of this course is to provide students from different disciplinary interests with the knowledge and hands-on skills in specific molecular microbial detection and characterization methods employed in the food and fermentation industries, environmental and other natural and man-made environments. The course will expose students to the fundamentals of microbial pathogen detection and associated molecular methods and provide a basis on how detection methods should be used for the different applications. The students will learn how to apply these methods in different scenarios and applications and how to interpret the results from such methods.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: BIOL 111 ; junior or senior classification. Cross Listing: FIVS 319/FSTC 319 .

title: Understanding Obesity - A Social and Scientific Challenge
description: Perspectives of obesity in food science, nutrition, health and psychology; study of obesity factors in relation to genetics, exercise physiology and sociology with emphasis on food and nutrition.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor. Cross Listing: NUTR 320/FSTC 320 .

title: Food Safety and Preventive Controls for Human Food
description: Microbiological food spoilage, fermentation and safety; U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) recognized curriculum for “preventive controls qualified individual” within the FDA Hazard Analysis and Risk‐based Preventive Controls for Human Food regulation.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.

title: Food Bacteriology
description: Microbiology of human foods and accessory substances; raw and processed foods; physical, chemical and biological phases of spoilage; standard industry techniques of inspection and control.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor. Cross Listing: ANSC 326/FSTC 326 .

title: Food Bacteriology Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany ANSC 326/FSTC 326 or FSTC 326/ANSC 326 .
prerequisites: Cross Listing: ANSC 327/FSTC 327 .

title: Electron Beam and Ionizing Technologies
description: Underlying theory of ionizing technologies cobalt-60 gamma, electron beam (eBeam) and X-ray technologies; focuses on the myriad of applications of these technologies in the agriculture, food, environment, medical industry, plastic polymers and other industries; environmental remediation, medical device sterilization, as well as agricultural industry applications in food safety, food quality and phytosanitary treatments.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.

title: Dairy and Food Technology
description: Principles and practices involved in processing of milk into market milk, butter, cheese and cheese foods; fundamental principles of these processes as related to their design and control.

title: Dairy and Food Technology
description: Manufacture of frozen, freeze-dehydrated, concentrated and dehydrated dairy foods; fundamental aspects of freezing, concentration and dehydration of foods.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: FSTC 330 or approval of department head.

title: Food Product Development
description: Design and develop food products using principles of food chemistry, food processing, nutrition, sensory analysis and statistics; team collaborate to improve food product characteristics to meet the needs of a changing society.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FSTC 201 , FSTC 311 , FSTC 312 , FSTC 313 , FSTC 314 , FSTC 315/AGSM 315 , FSTC 326/ANSC 326 , or concurrent enrollment; senior classification or approval of instructor.

title: Nutritional Pharmacometrics of Food Compounds
description: Nutritional pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of food compounds; specific examples of toxicological and pharmacological effects of food compounds.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: NUTR 201, NUTR 202 , NUTR 203 , CHEM 222 , or CHEM 227 , or approval of instructor; junior or senior classification. Cross Listing: NUTR 410/FSTC 410 .

title: Precision Fermentation and Future of Foods
description: Exploration of precision fermentation; bioprocessing to gene editing, and its applications in sustainable food production.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification.

title: Supervised Research in Mediterranean Nutrition and Food Processing in Italy
description: Exploration of principles of Mediterranean diet, European nutrition regulatory aspects, wine-making and food processing in Italy.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FSTC 201 , NUTR 202 , or NUTR 203 ; must be 18 years of age; class and tours taught in English; priority given to majors in FSTC or NUTR.

title: Food Processing for Sustainable Nutrition in Brazil
description: Sustainable nutrition and food processing in Brazil; hands-on learning at the Federal University of Vicosa, the Amazon Biotechnology Center, food processing plants and other research centers in the Amazon, central Brazil and Rio De Janeiro.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FSTC 201 , NUTR 202 , or NUTR 203 ; must be 18 years of age; class and tours taught in English; priority given to majors in FSTC or NUTR.

title: Innovative Functional Food Ingredients
description: Exploration of the impact of functional food ingredients on human health and the microbiome, processing, quality control, and regulatory compliance under FDA and FTC guidelines.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FSTC 201 and FSTC 311 , or FSTC 314 , or FSTC 313 ; or approval of instructor.

title: Fundamentals of Food Law
description: History, development of, and fundamental principles behind current food regulations, including food labeling, adulteration, food safety, food additives, dietary supplements, and import and export laws; overview of government agency jurisdiction, international law and ethics.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: FSTC 201 ; junior or senior classification.

title: Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point System
description: Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) principles specifically related to meat and poultry; microbiological and process overviews; good manufacturing practices and standard operating procedures development.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: FSTC 326/ANSC 326 or ANSC 326/FSTC 326 , or approval of instructor. Cross Listing: ANSC 457/FSTC 457 .

title: Quality Assurance for the Food Industry
description: Principles of food system process control including statistical process control (SPC) and the tools required to assure uniform communication and understanding of quality assurance systems.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification. Cross Listing: ANSC 470/FSTC 470 .

title: Seminar
description: Guidelines and practice in journal article review and making effective technical presentations; strategies for conducting a job search; development of résumés and letters and interviewing targeted for careers in the food industry or graduate school.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Senior classification in food science and technology.

title: Internship
description: Professional internship or practical food science experience in the food industry, non-profit organization, or other entity by instructor. Must be taken on a satisfactory/unsatisfactory basis.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification.

title: Directed Studies
description: Directed study on selected problems in the area of food science not covered in other courses.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification; approval of department head; 2.0 GPR in major and overall.

title: Sensory Evaluation of Foods
description: Application of sensory science principles and practices to food systems including an understanding of discriminative, descriptive and consumer sensory techniques.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: CHEM 222 or CHEM 228 ; junior or senior classification. Cross Listing: ANSC 487/FSTC 487 .

title: Special Topics in...
description: Selected topics in an identified area of food science and technology. May be repeated for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification.

title: Research
description: Research conducted under the direction of a faculty member in food science. May be repeated 3 times for credit. Registration in multiple sections of this course are possible within a given semester provided that the per semester credit hour limit is not exceeded.
repeatability: May be repeated 3 times for credit.
